title: Record that the 8-dimensional c=1 isotypic summand is reducible under…
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Exact proof over `Q` that the 8-dimensional isotypic summand inside the trivial-character `(+1,+1)` joint space of the historical `c=1` centre block is reducible under `A_1`.

The summand is the image of the projector for the linear character `ψ(r^k)=(-1)^k`, `ψ(r^k u)=(-1)^{k+1}` of the dihedral group generated by the signed permutations `r` and `u` recorded in PR #7008. On an explicit basis its characteristic polynomial is

```text
chi_{A_1}(x) = x^2 (x-2) (x+2) (x^2-2x-4) (x^2+2x-4).
```

As a `Q[A_1]`-module it is

```text
Q[x]/(x^2+2x-4) ⊕ Q[x]/(x^2-2x-4)
  ⊕ Q[x]/(x) ⊕ Q[x]/(x) ⊕ Q[x]/(x-2) ⊕ Q[x]/(x+2).
```

The two quadratic summands are irreducible. One explicit proper invariant subspace is the line `span{w4-w6}`, on which `A_1` acts by 0. No new kappa. The selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`.

## Task and overlap

- Task: `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed.
- Upstream base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`.
- Predecessor: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7008
- Finding this answers: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19507672
- Package: `research/a1-isotypic-8-split/`

The catalogue card asks for a formal caller binding. PR #7008 proved the ambient 216-space reducible under its signed normalizer and left this 8-dimensional summand unresolved. The character inner product gave the dimension and did not list a basis. This package builds the projector image and the matrix of `B=4 A_1`.

Overlap on 2026-11-10: 317 open PRs and 6971 discussion records, pagination complete; local notes 10180, HEAD paths 10178, complete. The phrases `8-dimensional isotypic`, `isotypic summand` and `multiplicity-8` matched only #7008. This package does not redo that normalizer census, the degree-216 characteristic polynomial of #6964, or the 8-dimensional joint spaces of the 32-dimensional `c=1` sign character.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/a1-isotypic-8-split/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/a1-isotypic-8-split/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a1-isotypic-8-split --check-only
```

Marker: `PASS_A1_ISOTYPIC_8_SPLIT`. Both modes passed. Metadata check returned `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Registered replay returned `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Selected baseline returned `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

The projector satisfies `(12P)^2 = 12(12P)`, has trace 96 and rank 8, and `r` and `u` act by `-I` on the image. The opposite linear character has rank 80. Rejection controls cover a coordinate transposition, the incomplete swap of coordinates 4 and 7, a swapped port label, a nearby change of `r`, a dropped support term, and a one-entry matrix change.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, the degree-216 characteristic polynomial, and the selected cold replay.

## Credit

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance.

JoyboyBrian recorded the sign-character dimensions. PR #6944 split the trivial `c=1` character into 216-dimensional blocks. PR #6964 pinned the basis and the characteristic polynomial of one 216-space. PR #7008 isolated this summand and left its irreducibility open. Ali Romman's PR4958 and PR4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Krzysztof Wojt's `research/exact-one-slot-gram/` supplies the degree-881 annihilator. Nick Petalas's PR5120 is the degree-410 lower bound. The doubled representation comes from PR1719. New work is Apache-2.0.
